subject: Signed image delivery & air-gapped update process — ACME Pharma readiness
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmepharma.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Signed images + offline update process (ACME)

Alice —

Per our call this morning, attached is the initial plan for delivering signed images for your air-gapped cluster and the proposed offline update process. High-level asks:

- Confirm the list of allowed hosts (we have the inventory from your security intake).
- Verify you can accept SHA256 manifest + detached signature (.sig) and the public key fingerprint we provide.
- Confirm maintenance window for the first rollout (we proposed 3 hours, low-traffic).

Attachments: image_manifest_v2.yaml (manifest of images + tags), signed_images_v2.tar.gz.sig (detached signature stub), airgap_release_checklist.pdf (operational checklist).

Next steps: if you can sign off on format and window, we will push the signed tarball to the offline transfer bucket and provide a transfer checklist and verification commands.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmepharma.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: SecOps Vendor <sec-ops@opssec.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Signed images + offline update process (ACME)

Vivek —

Thanks for the plan. A few quick clarifications before we book the maintenance window:

1) We require signatures to be verifiable with a hardware-backed key (HSM) or provide a certificate chain. Can you confirm the signing key origin?
2) Will the manifest include the image digests (sha256) for every layer, or only top-level image digest? Our scanner expects per-layer digs for evidence.
3) We need an explicit rollback artifact and a fast verification script (single-command, return code 0).

We can do a tentative window on 2026-08-02 22:00–01:00 UTC. Please confirm by EOD.

Best,
Alice Turner
Security Engineering Manager
ACME Pharmaceuticals
From: Registry Support <registry-support@corpimages.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T02:17:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Signed images + offline update process (ACME)

Hi team —

We have generated the detached signature for signed_images_v2.tar.gz and uploaded the tarball to the secure transfer area you requested. Notes:

- Signature format: OpenPGP detached signature (armor).
- Public key id: 0xA1B23C4D5E6F7890, fingerprint: 4D3A...7890 (full fingerprint in the attached key.txt).
- The manifest includes per-image digest and tag; per-layer digests are available on request as manifest_v2_layers.csv.

If you want a different signature format (COSE or PKCS7), we can re-run the signing pipeline; tell us which key id to use.

Regards,
Registry Support
CorpImages Registry
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-24T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: signing process and verification commands for ACME

Team —

Summary of steps I pushed to the release notes and the checklist:

1) Signing: we use our HSM-backed key (sig-key-2026) stored in KeyVault with attestations. The registry produced a detached OpenPGP signature; we validated fingerprint 4D3A...7890 against our CI key store.

2) Manifest: image_manifest_v2.yaml contains: image name, tag, top-level digest, and a per-image layers pointer file (manifest_v2_layers.csv). We included the signed manifest hash in the .sig to provide tamper evidence.

3) Verification commands (single-line examples for ACME ops team):

- Verify manifest signature (return 0 on success): gpg --verify signed_images_v2.tar.gz.sig image_manifest_v2.yaml
- Verify image digest locally after extraction: sha256sum --check manifest_v2_layers.csv

4) Rollback: signed_images_v2_rollback.tar.gz is created and signed. Rollback procedure in checklist is a single-step container restart pointing to the rollback tag; we added a healthcheck gate (3 successful readiness probes).

Attachments referenced in the release: signed_images_v2.tar.gz.sig, image_manifest_v2.yaml, signed_images_v2_rollback.tar.gz.sig on the transfer share.

Please review for gaps before I send the verification script to ACME directly.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-25T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: signing process and verification commands for ACME

On 2026-07-24, Dev Patel wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Summary of steps I pushed to the release notes and the checklist:
> 
> 1) Signing: we use our HSM-backed key (sig-key-2026) stored in KeyVault with attestations.

Thanks — two operational clarifications needed from SRE/Runtime:

- Upgrade window length: the checklist currently lists 3 hours. We should verify per-cluster sequential rolling strategy to avoid hitting peak memory when all nodes download artifacts. Propose we change the window to 4 hours for the first rollout and provide staggered node restart plan.
- Network: ACME will bring images via an air-gap transfer host. We must ensure the node-level agent can read local tarball paths without outbound network checks (disable remote registry pings during install). Add a flag in the installer (--offline-mode).

Also please attach the short verification script as a gist or inline so I can pass it to compliance.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: SecOps Vendor <sec-ops@opssec.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmepharma.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-27T14:36:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Signed images + offline update process (ACME)

Alice / Vivek —

We completed verification of the uploaded artifacts and signature fingerprint. Points to confirm before the rollout:

- Fingerprint match: registry key 4D3A...7890 verified against the signed key file.
- HSM attestation: OpsSec validated that sig-key-2026 is provisioned via the expected HSM vendor (YubiHSM). Attestation report attached (opssec_attestation_report.txt).
- Installer offline flag: our test of the installer with --offline-mode successfully avoided external fetches; it will read local manifests and run the sha256 checks.

One outstanding ask from compliance: can Redwood provide a deterministic checksum for the signed tarball contents (we recommend sha512) and a signed attestation stating the exact build IDs of images in the bundle.

Regards,
OpsSec Vendor
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acmepharma.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, SecOps Vendor <sec-ops@opssec.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: ACME air-gap rollout: final checklist and next steps

Team —

Thanks for the validation cycle — summary and action items:

- ACME confirmed maintenance window 2026-08-02 22:00–01:00 UTC.
- Dev to add sha512 deterministic checksum to the bundle and attach signed_attestation.txt (Dev: target 2026-07-30 EOD).
- Marissa to update checklist to a 4-hour window with staggered node restarts and include --offline-mode flag in installer (Marissa: target 2026-07-31).
- Registry/CorpImages to re-issue signatures in PKCS7 if ACME requests it (Registry: please standby).
- OpsSec: final attestation report will go into the ACME audit package.

Links: drive (release assets) and a one-line verification script are in the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/airgap/ACME-release-2026-07-22

Vivek
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
